body:
**Rivolt v0.40.16**

**Fixes**
- Rivolt no longer asks you to sign in to Rivian again right after you just did. A late reply from your old session could trigger it.
- When the truck sends no location during a drive, the drive page now says so instead of showing an empty map.

**Changes**
- The old public sample-trip pages now open the demo's trip planner.
- Clearer wording on the home page and charging-cost page during the beta.

**For self-hosters**
- Sign-in via a trusted proxy header has been removed. Use the normal sign-in.

**Rivolt v0.40.15**

**Fixes**
- Drive maps follow the road again where the truck's GPS dropped out, instead of drawing a straight line across the gap.
- The site now says plainly that Rivolt is free during the beta.

**Under the hood**
- More groundwork for one server per account, still switched off, so nothing changes in how Rivolt behaves today.
- Better counters for charging-schedule reads.

**Rivolt v0.40.14**

**New**
- Expecting an R2? The R2 page now has a short "before your R2 arrives" checklist, and you can ask for one email in your delivery month with the steps to connect it. It's off unless you choose a month, and the month is deleted once the email goes.

**Privacy**
- The privacy policy explains the R2 reminder: we keep only the month you pick, and delete it after sending.

**Fixes**
- Clearer wording about costs: Rivolt uses what Rivian billed where it can, otherwise your rate or a labelled estimate.
- The demo always shows sample data, even when you're signed in, and its first-charge example appears again.
- Trip planning gets priority when the server is busy right after an update, and charging schedules retry instead of being skipped.

**Under the hood**
- Groundwork for a year-in-review card in January.

**Rivolt v0.40.13**

**New**
- A week after your first charge, the first-charge card points you to Money, and to setting off-peak hours if you haven't yet.

**Fixes**
- The account deletion link from the iPhone app now lands on the right section even if you have to sign in first.
- Charging schedules read more reliably right after a server restart.

**Under the hood**
- Every write a vehicle's connection makes now checks which server owns that vehicle, groundwork for one server per account. It isn't switched on yet, so nothing changes in how Rivolt behaves today.
- Database connections are sized per server, and new alerts watch them.

**For self-hosters**
- Chart 0.16.2 works out the database pool size from the replica count (one replica keeps 20). With autoscaling on, set `dbConnections.systemMaxConns` explicitly.

**Rivolt v0.40.12**

**New**
- Money can offer to share what charging cost you this month. It appears once, and the cost stays hidden unless you add it.
- The "Is it safe to connect?" page is clearer about what Rivolt reads, what it keeps, and exactly how to sign out of Rivian.

**Under the hood**
- Updates now shut down more gently, so recording hands over cleanly between servers.
- More groundwork so a single server owns each Rivian connection. It isn't switched on yet, so nothing changes in how Rivolt behaves today.

**For self-hosters**
- The Helm chart (0.15.0) adds a pre-stop step and a 45-second shutdown grace period. Don't roll the image back below v0.40.11 without also reverting the chart.

**Rivolt v0.40.11**

**Under the hood**
- More groundwork so a single server owns each Rivian connection, for steadier recording during restarts. It isn't switched on yet, so nothing changes in how Rivolt behaves today.
- A temporary clean-up of old Rivian tokens has finished its job and is removed.

**For self-hosters**
- An unknown command-line argument now exits with an error instead of starting the server.

**Rivolt v0.40.10**

**Fixes**
- The "See a planned trip first" link on the home page now opens the Los Angeles to Las Vegas sample trip straight away. Before, it showed "This sample trip didn't load" until you reloaded. The same fix applies to the trip links on the charging networks page.

**Rivolt v0.40.9**

**New**
- **Five new sample road trips:** Seattle–Portland, Denver–Moab, San Francisco–Lake Tahoe, Los Angeles–Phoenix and New York–Boston, each showing times in its own time zone.
- **A first-week guide for R2 owners** at /r2: what's recorded today and what isn't yet.
- **Compare charging networks** at /charging-networks.
- **Optional trip recap notification:** after you drive a saved trip, see how it went. It's off by default; turn it on in Settings → Notifications.
- **A one-time prompt on Money** to add your off-peak hours, if you have a home rate set without them.

**Privacy**
- The connect step now says up front what Rivolt reads (such as drives, charges, battery and location), that it never sends commands to your truck, and that your Rivian password is never stored.
- The privacy page mentions the trip recap notification (updated Oct 28).

**Under the hood**
- Groundwork so a single server owns each Rivian connection, for steadier recording during restarts.

**Rivolt v0.40.8**

**New**
- **A heads-up before your Rivian connection expires.** Rivian sign-ins last about 6 months. A week before yours ends, Rivolt shows "Your Rivian connection expires <date>." with a Reconnect link, on the web and in the iPhone app. Settings → Rivian account shows the date too.

**Privacy**
- Deleting your account now also clears your live vehicle snapshot and planner counters right away, instead of letting them expire within a few hours.
- Rivolt no longer requests or stores two Rivian tokens it never used.

**Fixes**
- Trip-planner and Rivian request limits now hold steady even during a brief internal outage.
- Waking a plugged-in truck no longer logs a blip "charge" of a second or two. These never showed in your lists, but they inflated charge counts and, rarely, sent a false "Charging complete" alert.

**Rivolt v0.40.7**

**Fixes**
- **Reconnecting your Rivian account works reliably.** After you sign in to Rivian again, Rivolt no longer keeps saying "needs re-login" on some page loads, and no stray "reconnect" email follows.
- **The Rivian sign-in form stays put while you type.** It no longer disappears or resets mid-entry.
- **Clearer sign-in recovery.** If a Rivolt sign-in took too long or was started in another tab, you get a "Start sign-in again" button.
- **Privacy:** turning off recap weather now takes effect everywhere within seconds.

**Rivolt v0.40.6**

**Improvements**
- **Flat-rate electricity:** if you've said your rate is flat, the Off-peak savings card no longer appears on Money.
- **Period picker on phones:** opening it no longer squeezes the page title.
- **iPhone app support:** the app can now change your off-peak schedule, flat-rate setting, charging network prices and trip planner defaults (gas price and MPG included). Applying a rate to past charges stays on the website.

**Rivolt v0.40.5**

**Fixes**
- **Notifications on Chrome Beta, Dev and Canary:** turning notifications on no longer fails with "unsupported push service". If notifications can't be turned on in your browser, the page now says so plainly instead of looking switched on.
- **Truck sleep chart:** dates read like "Oct 1" and the hour marks are round numbers.
- **Period picker on phones:** the open panel no longer covers the page's own tabs.
- **Drive maps:** the route's end marker no longer sits under the speed legend.

**Rivolt v0.40.4**

**New**
- **Pick the period you want:** on Now, Activity and Truck, choose Day, Week, Month or Custom. Day starts on today, and the arrows step back one day at a time. "This year" and "All time" are one tap away inside Custom, and views you saved before still open.

**Improvements**
- **Charts are easier to read:** axis labels are smaller and lighter than the data, ticks use round numbers (0 · 200 · 400 instead of 509 and 255), and dates read like "Oct 1" in your language.
- **No more overlapping "0":** the baseline no longer shows a "0" or "0%" that collided with the first date.

**iPhone app** (TestFlight): the same period picker and chart changes.

**Rivolt v0.40.3**

**Fixes**
- **Drive map:** the speed key is now a small corner chip that shows only the speeds that drive reached.
- **Consistent text sizes:** every label on a map uses one size, and the remaining one-off text sizes across the site now follow a single scale. Some small labels grow by about one pixel.

**Rivolt v0.40.2**

**Fixes**
- **Demo:** months you open more than once load again on the website and in the iPhone app. A repeat request was being sent back compressed twice, so it came through unreadable. Signed-in accounts were not affected.

**Rivolt v0.40.1**

**Fixes**
- **iPhone app sign-in page:** the Cancel button is readable again in dark mode.
- **Demo:** browsing months and tabs quickly no longer hits "couldn't load".
- **Hotels with no charger:** the nearby fast charger now reads "right next to it" when it's within a short walk, and power is shown only when the listing gives it.

**Rivolt v0.40.0**

**New**
- **Better places to stay on long trips:** the two-day planner now follows the actual road when it looks for a hotel or campground with a charger, so it finds more of them.
- **Hotels near a fast charger:** where no stay lists a charger, Rivolt can suggest a nearby hotel with no charger and plan the next morning's first stop at the closest fast charger. It's always labelled "No charger listed here".
- **"Nearest listed stay":** when nothing fits the day, you see how far back or ahead the nearest listed stay is, instead of just "none".
- **Arrival times on the destination's clock,** with the time zone named when it differs from yours.

**iPhone app** (TestFlight): the full trip planner, saved trips, plan vs actual, per-day stops for two-day trips, and a read-only passkeys list.

Hotel listings © OpenStreetMap contributors.

**Rivolt v0.39.10**

- **Privacy page:** a new section explains what Rivolt stores if you use passkeys, ahead of sign-in with passkeys. Your fingerprint, face and the passkey's private key never leave your device.

**Rivolt v0.39.9**

- **New Security tab in Settings:** change your password, or reset it and remove all passkeys in one step if you think someone else got in. Either way your other devices are signed out and you get an email.
- **Shorter signed-in devices list:** your recent browsers are shown, with "Show all" for the rest. "Sign out everywhere else" still signs out every one.
- **Stronger passwords:** new passwords must be at least 8 characters and can't be your email address.
- **Privacy:** our diagnostic traces no longer record your IP address or browser.

**For self-hosters:**
- Docker builds from the repository work again.
- Rivolt no longer accepts an Ory Kratos session cookie as a sign-in. Set `RIVOLT_ACCEPT_KRATOS_COOKIE=true` only if your own setup signs users in through Kratos's browser flow; Rivolt then also requires `RIVOLT_KRATOS_COOKIE_HOST`.

**Rivolt v0.39.8**

A security fix for signing out.

- **Signing out now fully signs you out.** Before, a browser that had signed in within the last day could click Sign in after signing out and get straight back in without a password. Now it has to enter the password again. This also covers "Sign out other devices" and signing out a single device from your devices list.
- **Passkeys (not switched on yet):** a clear message if a passkey no longer works, and no failed background request on Settings.

**Rivolt v0.39.7**

A behind-the-scenes release: nothing changes on your screens.

- **Stronger separation between accounts:** groundwork so the database itself can keep each account's data apart, on top of the checks the app already makes.
- **Safer updates:** database updates can now run as a separate step before a new version starts, so a failed update can't take the site down.
- **Notifications:** registering an iPhone for notifications is checked more strictly across accounts.
- **Coming soon:** sign-in with passkeys is built but stays switched off for now.

**Rivolt v0.39.6**

- **One units setting for your account:** miles or kilometres, °F or °C, saved to your account and used everywhere you sign in. Change it in Settings → Vehicle → Display. The first time, it starts from your device's region; your own pick always wins.
- **Efficiency, trends and cold-weather range** follow that setting too.
- **Clearer message** when a truck isn't connected to Rivian yet, instead of a server error.
- **iPhone app (next TestFlight):** a Units screen in the account menu, home location and vehicle details editable in the app, and real map tiles in the demo.

**Rivolt v0.39.5**

- **Now updates after a drive:** "Since last charge" and Miles refresh by themselves in the minutes after a drive or charge ends, instead of showing the old numbers until you reopen the page.
- **Kilometres in the trip planner:** with km selected, multi-day plans show km everywhere (totals, day headers, legs, warnings).
- **Tire warning:** the low-tire banner on Now shows two decimals in bar, like the Tires card.

**Rivolt v0.39.4**

- **Trip planner, long routes:** chargers along a cross-country route now load in about a second instead of up to half a minute, and no longer time out. Switching between Fast charging, Level 2, hotels and campgrounds is quick too.
- **iPhone notifications:** a phone's notification registration can no longer be moved to another account by someone else. Switching accounts on your own phone works as before.

**Rivolt v0.39.3**

- **Trip planner, long routes:** cross-country trips plan without the "query is too large" error, and chargers along very long routes load.
- **Overnight stops:** the search looks further around your 8-hour point. When nothing is found it says how far it looked; a stay away from that point says how far before or after it is (in km if you use metric).
- **Plainer charger words:** "Fast charging" and "Level 2" instead of DCFC and L2.
- **Now card:** cabin temperature gets its own row, like outside; both in whole degrees.
- **Tires card:** pressure in bar shows two decimals, so nearby readings no longer look the same.
- **New support page** at rivolt.dev/support, linked from the footer.
- **Privacy page** updated (Oct 24): we use AI tools to help run and repair Rivolt.
- **Terms** are now also enforced by the server, not just the website. Export and account deletion always stay available.

**Fixes**
- The trip map shows chargers along long routes again. Since Oct 18, routes over roughly 1,000 km showed no chargers on the map (the route was refused as too detailed); long routes are now simplified instead.
- Faster Now page and app: a background query that re-read your truck's whole history on every refresh now reads only the recent week.

**Fixes**
- Time left while charging uses your truck's own estimate (time to your charge limit) when it's trustworthy; otherwise Rivolt's estimate, marked "est.".
- The live charging card's "cost so far" now comes from the charge's own energy. A charge that had just started could briefly show a cost left over from an earlier session.
- No home-rate "cost so far" estimate on fast charging or charging away from home.

**Sprint 8: more from your truck's own data**
- **Tires card** on the Truck tab: four pressures and how old the reading is. A tire is marked "Low" below 32 psi or when the truck itself says low.
- **Sleep health:** "Nothing unusual this week" or "Woke N more times than usual this week", compared only with your truck's own last 30 days.
- **Trailer on drives:** drives with a trailer connected are tagged, left out of your efficiency figures (and it says how many), and you can correct a drive.
- **Left-open alert** (opt-in, web and iPhone): a door, frunk, liftgate, tailgate or tonneau open 15 minutes after parking. Windows aren't covered.
- **Comfort line on Now** while the truck is live: cabin temperature, pet mode, climate hold, preconditioning.
- **Software update status** in the truck's own words.
- **Estimated charges are marked** with "~", and the October statement says so.

Not in this release: a tire-pressure alert, a charge time estimate from the truck, an update progress percentage.

The demo at demo.rivolt.dev now shows the Tires card and, from Oct 28, a trailer drive.

**New**
- Sleep health on the Truck tab: "Nothing unusual this week" or "Woke N more times than usual this week", compared only with your truck's own last 30 days.
- Trailer on drives: drives with a trailer connected are tagged, left out of your efficiency figures (with a note saying how many), and you can correct a drive on its page.
- Estimated charges are marked: when a charge's energy had to be estimated from the battery's change, its kWh and cost show with "~", and the monthly statement says so.

**Fixes**
- Sign-in buttons always appear in the same order: Email, Google, GitHub.
- Plan vs actual reads "Why:" before its reasons, and the demo no longer suggests saving a route.
- Faster background statistics, with less load on the database.

**Self-hosting**
- Runtime images are pinned by digest.

**Correction (Oct 24)**
- Some home charges since Oct 15 recorded too little energy because of a bug. We've corrected them from the battery's change, so their cost may be higher; they're marked as estimated.

**Fixes**
- Home charges no longer lose recorded energy when Rivolt's server restarts or hands a truck over mid-charge. Since Oct 15 some home charges recorded too little energy, so their cost showed too low.
- If a charge's measured energy still comes out far below what the battery's change implies, Rivolt now estimates it from the battery's change and marks it as estimated.
- Past affected charges were corrected on Oct 24 (see v0.38.28): their energy now comes from the battery's change, so their cost may be higher, and they're marked as estimated.

**New**
- Left-open alert: an opt-in notification when a door, the frunk, liftgate, tailgate or tonneau stays open 15 minutes while the truck is parked. Off until you turn it on in Settings, Notifications. Windows aren't covered.
- Tires card on the Truck tab: all four pressures with the time of the last reading.
- Flat-rate electricity: if your plan has no off-peak hours, set one rate in Settings.
- Software update status on the Truck tab (downloading, ready to install, installing) when your truck reports one.

**Changed**
- One look everywhere: the old look is gone, and the sign-in, legal and calculator pages now match the app.
- Plan vs actual explains every reason and the dotted estimate again, and says what to do when you have no saved trips yet. The demo planner shows its "Sample plan" label.

**Privacy**
- The privacy page now lists whether a trailer is connected (recorded for an upcoming efficiency split) and the left-open alert.

**Self-hosting**
- The Docker image now builds with Go 1.27.3, matching the release binaries.

One Battery capacity card, a Truck summary, and cabin status on Now.

- Truck: a single "Battery capacity" card. The headline is what your truck reports as usable; under it, Rivolt's own estimate from your charges ("about 122 kWh, from 5 charges") and Rivian's spec for the pack. The chart now shows one dot per charge (bigger for larger charges) with a trend only where charges are close together, instead of lines across empty months.
- Truck: a one-line summary at the top: usable pack and parked drain (last 7 days).
- Now: a quiet line with cabin temperature, pet mode, climate hold and preconditioning, shown only while your truck's data is current.
- Now: your truck's card comes first; tips and milestones sit below it.

A calmer Battery chart, and release notes that open.

- The Battery (SoC) trend is redrawn: a soft band shows each day's lowest-to-highest level, one smooth line shows where the day ended, and only the month's highest and lowest points are labelled. Road trips read as a peak or a dip instead of spikes; the charge limit shows from its last change to today; small ticks mark the days you charged.
- "Release notes" for your truck's software now opens: Rivolt fetches a fresh link from Rivian when you tap it (the old one expired after an hour).

Privacy
- Rivian's release-notes links carried temporary access credentials; Rivolt no longer stores them, and the stored ones were removed.

Rivolt is now run by ZeroDowntime LLC.

- The Terms and Privacy Policy name ZeroDowntime LLC, a Texas limited liability company, as the operator. Nothing changes about the service or your data.
- Questions, privacy requests and security reports now go to support@rivolt.dev.

Fixes
- Saving a charge's Home/Away choice or pin shows a plain "Couldn't save" message instead of a technical error.
- The phone app can change your home charging rate (needs the next TestFlight build).

Your charges, your call.

- Mark a charge Home or Away yourself, and pin it where the truck actually was instead of the nearest public charger. Your choices stay put when your home location changes.
- Networks you add yourself can have a location, so charges there are labelled and offered that network's rate.
- Home address search no longer shows duplicate suggestions, and says "Searching…" while it looks.

Fixes
- New accounts without a connected Rivian no longer see an error when loading their trucks.
- Self-hosting docs now explain street-level address search.

Home location and phone security.

- Set your home precisely: type coordinates, search a street address, or use one of your charges as home (Settings, on the web). You'll see which past charges would change before anything is re-labelled, and you can undo it.
- The iPhone app can now change your home charging rate (the app screen arrives in a coming TestFlight build).

Privacy and security
- The iPhone app's sign-in can now only do what the app needs (notifications, the charging Live Activity, signing out, hiding milestones, and your home rate). It can't change your account, privacy settings or Rivian connection, export your data, or force a fresh read from your truck.
- The privacy page now says your home location is stored as exactly as you set it.

Battery trend, clearer.

- The Battery (SoC) trend now uses a straight line between readings and covers the whole calendar month, with dates on the 1st, 11th, 21st and the last day.
- A thin strip under the chart shows when the truck was charging or driving.
- The charge limit is drawn as steps: it changes on the day you changed it, using the limit each charge actually had.
- Each charge now remembers the charge limit it was set to, including charges from before this update.

Map server hardening.

- Map tile requests must ask for a small, specific piece of the map; anything else is refused before it reaches the map server.
- Route matching, which the next iPhone update uses to draw drives on the roads, now has firm size limits and only accepts the request shapes the apps send.

Nothing changes in how maps look or work.

Map tile protections.

- Map tiles can now only be downloaded in small pieces, the way maps actually use them. A trick that let one request download the whole map file is closed.
- The public demo site has a fair-use data allowance per visitor, so nobody can pull large amounts of map data from it.
- The battery history behind the Truck page can be fetched in smaller pieces, so the phone downloads less.

Nothing changes in how maps look or work.

Small web fixes, and server support for the iPhone Money tab.

- Links to a Settings card on a phone now land with the card's heading visible, clear of the header, and the last row stays above the bottom tab bar.
- Every Settings card link opens its own tab. Some used to open the Account tab with no card.
- Links to cards that load a moment later, such as setup emails and the weekly recap, now land on the card every time.
- A new, smaller feed for the Money tab's "To confirm" list. It carries no locations.

Server support for the next iPhone app update.

- Drive and charge lists can be filtered to one truck, so two-truck households see the right truck's last drive and charge.
- New small data feeds for the iPhone's Home charts (miles per day, charge level, idle time), the Home / Away / Fast charging split, and the Activity list. They carry no locations.
- These feeds have a fair-use limit per account, so a misbehaving app can't slow things down for everyone.
- Fixed a test that occasionally failed for no real reason.

Nothing changes on the website.

## What's new

- **Live charging on your iPhone's Lock Screen (TestFlight).** Turn on "Live Activity while charging" in the app, and while your truck charges the Lock Screen (and Dynamic Island) shows charge level, power and minutes to your limit. Off until you turn it on, per iPhone.

## Privacy

- The privacy policy now covers live charging on the Lock Screen: what's kept and for how long (until the charge ends, at most 13 hours), and that Apple receives only the charge level, power and minutes to your limit, never your truck's location, name or VIN. Last updated October 21, 2026.

## What's new

- **Rivolt for iPhone is coming (invite-only TestFlight).** The server side is ready: signing in from the app through rivolt.dev, a list of your signed-in devices, and iPhone notifications. The app itself is in internal testing.

## Privacy

- The privacy policy now covers the iPhone app: the device type it reports for your list of signed-in devices, your phone's Apple push address (deleted when you turn notifications off or sign the phone out), and Apple's push service, which only ever sees a random number and "Rivolt update", never the text. Last updated October 21, 2026.

## Fixes

- The sign-in confirmation page shows your account's email correctly.

## What's new

- **Campgrounds now always get a spot in overnight suggestions.** When a federal campground with an electric hookup is within reach of your overnight stop, one of the three suggestions is the best one, next to Level 2 hotels.

## Fixes

- **On phones, the trip summary no longer covers the campground card.** The reservation note and the Recreation.gov credit can be scrolled into view at any sheet height.
- **Faster repeat visits:** app files are now cached properly by your browser.

## Fixes

- **No more blank page right after an update.** If you opened Rivolt while we were deploying, a page could fail to load until you refreshed. It now recovers by itself.

## Behind the scenes

- More groundwork for the Rivolt iPhone app (signed-in devices and notifications). It stays switched off until the app ships, and nothing changes for you today.

## What's new

- **Demo:** the off-peak savings card on demo.rivolt.dev now says plainly that it uses the sample truck and an example schedule.

## Behind the scenes

- Groundwork for the Rivolt iPhone app (sign-in and notifications). It stays switched off until the app ships, and nothing changes for you today.

## What's new

- **Off-peak hours.** In Settings → Charging, add your utility's off-peak windows (weekday and weekend, past midnight, with a rate for each). Rivolt uses them only for estimates and never contacts your utility.
- **What off-peak could have saved.** Money shows an estimate of what moving last month's home charging into your off-peak windows could have saved, and which sessions were left out and why. It's advice only, and Rivolt never changes charging on your truck.
- **Savings in your monthly email**, as one estimate line when you have a schedule.
- **Download the month as CSV**: totals by cost type, home versus away, and one line per session.
- **Off-peak share on share cards**: an optional line, with a switch that is off every time.
- **Membership plan terms** under Charging networks, each with its source and the date it was last checked.
- **New public page:** [How much does it cost to charge a Rivian at home?](https://rivolt.dev/charging-cost), a calculator that needs no sign-in.

## What's new

- **Add your own overnight stop.** In the trip planner, add any place as an overnight and pick its hookup: a J1772 station, or a NEMA 14-50 RV outlet with Rivian's Portable Charger (planned at 7.2 kW). Slow 30 A and 120 V outlets are marked as such.
- **Federal campgrounds with electric hookups** can now appear next to Level 2 hotels as overnight options, with data from Recreation.gov. They start showing after the next charger-data refresh.
- **Clearer charging power.** When a station offers more than your truck can take, the plan shows the power your truck will actually use.
- **"Billed by Rivian"** now labels charges priced from your Rivian receipt.

## What's new

- **Honest fast-charging prices.** Fast-charging sessions without your own rate are now estimated from a typical price (DCFC Tracker), not an old table. Add the rate you pay for exact costs. Money shows estimated sessions and sessions that still need a price on their own lines.
- **Set your rate once, price the past.** After you add a network's rate in Settings, "Price earlier sessions at this rate" fills in estimated and unpriced sessions. It never touches a bill or a price you entered.
- **Rivian bills win.** With charging receipts turned on, a session Rivian billed shows the billed amount everywhere.
- **More overnight options.** Bed-and-breakfasts with Level 2 charging now appear next to hotels in the trip planner.

## Fixes

- Settings no longer shows old default network prices as if they were yours.
- Sample trips link each typical price to its source.

## Fixes

- **Honest charging prices in the trip planner.** Fast-charging stops are no longer priced from an old mid-2025 table. Each stop now uses your own Rivian receipts (if you've turned them on), then a dated typical price from DCFC Tracker, and otherwise says "price shown at the charger". Trip costs show as a range.
- **Correct membership names.** EVgo Plus, Shell Recharge Rewards and "Rivian owner discount" replace three plan names we had wrong, including in rates you saved earlier.

## Fixes

- **Drives and Charges on phones.** The page no longer scrolls sideways on narrow screens; the view and date-range buttons now wrap onto a second line.

## Privacy

- **Maps no longer pass on your IP address.** Map tiles and route planning go through our own servers, and those servers now never receive your IP address.

## Behind the scenes

- Code checks now run on every change, and the issues they found are fixed.

## What's new

- **Parked-drain split on quiet weeks.** If the last 7 days don't have enough parked time, the card switches to the last 30 days and says so.
- **Battery capacity wording.** The "not enough data yet" line no longer lists a time span that's already met.

## Demo

- The demo now has enough history for the trends, battery capacity and range-by-temperature cards to draw.

## Behind the scenes

- Routine dependency updates, plus faster, more reliable automatic updates.

## What's new

- **R2: asleep vs awake.** The parked-drain card now shows how much of the battery lost while parked went while the truck was awake, for the R2 too. Sleep and power state are now confirmed on real R2s.

## Behind the scenes

- Groundwork for the coming long-term archive and database monitoring.

## Behind the scenes

- The parked-drain calculation uses less disk on the server.

## Fixes

- **Your data export now includes everything:** saved trips, trip recaps, efficiency analyses, milestones and the weather stored for your drives. Backups now include saved trips, milestones, recaps and analyses too, and restoring the same backup twice never duplicates them.
- Text you type, such as saved-trip names, always shows exactly as typed.

## Behind the scenes

- The parked-drain calculation no longer writes large temporary files to disk on every run.

## Hardening complete
